claimChallenged: Parmana's core invariant that no unauthorized action executes: policy was evaluated against caller-declared signals that nothing bound to the Intent the gateway actually signs and executes (docs/VERIFICATION-GAPS.md G-24, 04-INCIDENTS-LOG.md INC-6).

source.attribution: An external adversarial security exercise against a disposable local clone; the tester is not named in the repository.

investigationSteps.method: Live proof of concept through POST /execute with a valid API key and no other privilege, on an isolated clone and again on this repository after the fix: signals declared an approved 5000 payment to VENDOR-1001 while the intent targeted ATTACKER-CONTROLLED-ACCOUNT-9999 for 999999999. The exact date is not recorded; this is the latest date the cited sources support.
investigationSteps.observation: Before the fix: 200, APPROVED, COMPLETED, with a signed Execution Trust Record and receipt. Same session: any key could claim any authority.principalId, and any caller could read any other caller's transactions and records (IDOR).

finding.statement: A live, reproducible bypass of the no-unauthorized-execution invariant, with signed evidence attesting to an action that never happened as described; the most severe gap in docs/VERIFICATION-GAPS.md.

outcome.description: Policy.boundSignals and SignalIntentBinder refuse a request whose bound signals do not match the executed Intent, before evaluation; isPrincipalAllowed binds authority.principalId to the API key; isOwnedByCaller scopes every read route to its caller. Later, signed human approvals (2.42, 2.47) replaced caller-declared facts as the authorizing signal.

disclosure.location: docs/VERIFICATION-GAPS.md G-24 and 04-INCIDENTS-LOG.md INC-6, in this public repository
